name: Sous vide
summary: Food is sealed in a bag and cooked in a water bath at an exact low temperature, so that the whole piece reaches the same core heat.
how: Season the food and seal it in a bag with the air removed.
Set the water bath to the target core temperature, for example 56 °C for beef.
Cook for the time that the thickness of the piece needs, from 1 to 48 hours.
Chill or sear the food just before service.

origin.note: Georges Pralus cooked foie gras in a sealed bag for the Troisgros kitchen to lose less fat.

adoptions.via: Chefs of the avant-garde kitchen, such as Heston Blumenthal, took the water bath into the tasting menu.
The book Modernist Cuisine gave tables of time and temperature for each food.
